extracted.intended_audience: corporate counsel, SEC reporting teams, compliance officers and public company management
extracted.subtask_description: A practical checklist of events that trigger a Form 8-K disclosure obligation under the Exchange Act, with required filing/furnishing periods, S-3 eligibility impacts, and special instructions or exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 1.01 — Entry into a material definitive agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrant enters into a material definitive agreement not made in the ordinary course of business or into an amendment of such agreement that is material to registrant; see Reg S-K Item 601(b)(10) (excluding (iii)(A) and (B), management or compensatory agreements or arrangements, which, as to the principal executive officer, principal financial officer or other named executive officers, are covered under Item 5.02).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing period: Within 4 business days. S-3 impact: No impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 1.02 — Termination of a material definitive agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: A material definitive agreement not made in the ordinary course of business of registrant terminates (other than by expiration on a stated termination date, or the completion of all parties’ obligations) where such termination is material to registrant; see Reg S-K Item 601(b)(10) (excluding (iii)(A) and (B), management or compensatory agreements or arrangements, which, as to the principal executive officer, principal financial officer or other named executive officers, are now covered under Item 5.02).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing period: Within 4 business days of termination, or notice of termination pursuant to the terms of the agreement. S-3 impact: No impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 1.03 — Bankruptcy or receivership
rubrics_metrics.description: Appointment of a receiver, fiscal agent or similar officer for registrant or its parent in a bankruptcy proceeding (federal or state); entry of an order confirming a plan of reorganization, arrangement or liquidation relating to registrant’s or its parent’s assets or business by a court or governmental authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing period: Within 4 business days. S-3 impact: Yes — failure to timely file will impact S-3 eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 1.04 — Mine safety: reporting of shutdowns and patterns of violations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registrant or a subsidiary receives, with respect to a coal or other mine of which the registrant or subsidiary is an operator: (a) an imminent danger order issued under Section 107(a) of the Mine Safety Act; (b) a written notice from MSHA that the Mine has a pattern of violations under Section 104(e); or (c) a written notice from MSHA that the Mine has the potential to have such a pattern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing period: Within 4 business days. S-3 impact: No impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 1.05 — Material Cybersecurity Incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registrant experiences a cybersecurity incident that is determined by the registrant to be material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing period: Within 4 business days of the company making the determination that the cybersecurity incident was material. Registrant may delay filing where the U.S. Attorney General has notified the SEC in writing that disclosure poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety. S-3 impact: No impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 2.01 — Completion of acquisition or disposition of assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrant or a consolidated subsidiary completes an acquisition or disposition of a 'significant amount of assets' (otherwise than in the ordinary course of business), or a 'significant amount of assets' that constitute a real estate operation as defined in Regulation S-X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing period: Within 4 business days. S-3 impact: Yes — failure to timely file will impact S-3 eligibility. Instruction: 'Significant amount of assets' generally means (i) equity in net book value or amount paid/received exceeded 10% of total assets, (ii) involved a business significant to registrant or a majority-owned subsidiary (includes equity method investments or fair value option), or (iii) for business development companies, amount paid exceeded 10% of total investments. 'Business' and 'significant' are defined in Regulation S-X.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 2.02 — Results of operations and financial condition (furnished)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrant (or person acting on its behalf) publicly announces or releases material non-public information regarding registrant’s results of operations or financial condition for a completed quarterly or annual fiscal period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Furnishing period: Within 4 business days; must be furnished before an oral/telephonic broadcast or webcast complementary to the Form 8-K and occurring within 48 hours of the furnishing if the broadcast/webcast complements a widely disseminated press release to avoid having to furnish an additional Form 8-K. S-3 impact: No impact. Note: Information in this item is 'furnished' (not 'filed') for purposes of Section 18 of the Exchange Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 2.03 — Creation of a direct financial obligation or off-balance sheet obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrant becomes obligated on a direct financial obligation that is material to it or becomes directly or contingently liable for a material obligation arising out of an off-balance sheet arrangement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing period: Within 4 business days. No filing requirement for obligations that are registered securities if described in a prospectus timely filed under Rule 424. Registrant may delay filing if neither it nor an affiliate is a party to the transaction or agreement creating the contingent obligation until the earlier of (i) the fourth business day after the contingent obligation is created or arises and (ii) the day an executive officer becomes aware of the contingent obligation. S-3 impact: No impact. Instruction: A material facility, program or similar arrangement requires disclosure upon entry if material, as obligations arise if material, or as individually immaterial obligations become material in the aggregate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 2.04 — Triggering events that accelerate or increase financial obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Occurrence of a triggering event causing an increase or acceleration of a direct financial obligation, the consequences of which are material to registrant; or causing an obligation under an off-balance sheet arrangement to increase/be accelerated or a contingent obligation to become a direct financial obligation (including an accrual for probable loss under ASC 450), where consequences are material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing period: Within 4 business days. S-3 impact: No impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 2.05 — Costs associated with exit or disposal activities
rubrics_metrics.description: If registrant’s board, a committee or an authorized officer commits registrant to an exit or disposal plan, otherwise disposes of a long-lived asset, or terminates employees under a plan of termination described in ASC 420, under which material charges will be incurred under GAAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing period: Within 4 business days. Registrant may delay filing if terminating employees as part of a plan to exit an activity until it has informed affected employees. S-3 impact: No impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 2.06 — Material impairments
rubrics_metrics.description: If registrant’s board, a committee or an authorized officer concludes that a material charge for impairment to one or more assets (including impairments of securities or goodwill) is required under GAAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing period: Within 4 business days. No filing required if impairment determination is made in connection with preparation, review or audit of financial statements at period end and is disclosed in the timely-filed periodic report for that period. S-3 impact: No impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 3.01 — Notice of delisting or failure to satisfy continued listing standard; transfer of listing
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrant receives notice from its principal national securities exchange or association that registrant or a class of securities does not satisfy a rule/standard for continued listing, the exchange submitted an application to the SEC to delist registrant’s securities, or the association has taken steps to delist; or registrant notifies its exchange/association it is aware of material noncompliance; or exchange/association issues public reprimand; or registrant takes definitive action to withdraw/terminate listing or transfer listing to another exchange/quotation system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing period: Within 4 business days. S-3 impact: Yes — failure to timely file will impact S-3 eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 3.02 — Unregistered sales of equity securities
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrant sells its equity securities in a transaction not registered under the Securities Act, including conversions and similar transactions that equal or exceed, in the aggregate, 1% (or 5% if registrant is a smaller reporting company) of outstanding shares.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing period: Within 4 business days of entry into an enforceable agreement, or, if no agreement, after closing or settlement. S-3 impact: Yes — failure to timely file will impact S-3 eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 3.03 — Material modification to rights of security holders
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrant’s constituent instruments defining the rights of holders of any class of registered securities are materially modified; or the rights of any class are materially limited or qualified by issuance/modification of any other class of securities by registrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing period: Within 4 business days. S-3 impact: Yes — failure to timely file will impact S-3 eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 4.01 — Changes in registrant’s certifying accountant
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrant’s principal accountant, or an independent accountant upon whom the principal accountant expressed reliance regarding a significant subsidiary, resigns, is dismissed or declines to stand for re-appointment after completion of the current audit; or registrant engages a new independent accountant as principal accountant or as an independent accountant expected to be relied upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing period: Within 4 business days. S-3 impact: Yes — failure to timely file will impact S-3 eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 4.02 — Non-reliance on previously issued financial statements or related audit report (or completed interim review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrant’s board, committee or authorized officer concludes previously issued annual or interim financial statements should no longer be relied upon because of an error as addressed in ASC 250; or registrant is advised by or receives notice from its independent accountant that disclosure should be made or action taken to prevent future reliance on a previously issued audit report or completed interim review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing period: Within 4 business days. For disclosures required under the non-italicized bullet, registrant must amend its previously filed Form 8-K by filing the independent accountant's letter as an exhibit no later than 2 business days after registrant's receipt of the letter. S-3 impact: Yes — failure to timely file will impact S-3 eligibility unless the report relates only to the matter described in the italicized bullet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 5.01 — Changes in control of registrant
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrant’s board, committee or an authorized officer knows that a change in control of registrant has occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing period: Within 4 business days. S-3 impact: Yes — failure to timely file will impact S-3 eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 5.02 — Departure/election/appointment of directors or certain officers; compensatory arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Directors: resignation/refusal to stand for re-election because of a disagreement with registrant known to an executive officer, removal for cause, retirement/resignation/refusal to stand for re-election or election of a new director (except by stockholder vote at an annual/special meeting). Officers: retirement, resignation or termination of principal executive officer, president, principal financial officer, principal accounting officer, principal operating officer or similar; appointment of new such officers. Registrant: enters into/commences a material compensatory plan/contract/arrangement involving named executive officers or materially amends such arrangements; makes or materially modifies a material grant/award; makes a payment/grant/award or other decision that makes amount of salary/bonus of a named executive officer calculable when previously not calculable (and therefore omitted from Summary Compensation Table).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing period: Within 4 business days. Filing regarding officer appointment may be delayed until registrant’s first public announcement regarding the appointment, if announcement will be other than by Form 8-K. For director disclosures under the first bullet, registrant must amend previously filed Form 8-K by filing director's letter (if any) as an exhibit no later than 2 business days after registrant's receipt of the letter. S-3 impact: Yes — failure to timely file will impact S-3 eligibility unless report relates only to matters described in the italicized bullets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 5.03 — Amendments to articles of incorporation or bylaws; change in fiscal year
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrant amends its articles of incorporation or bylaws and a proposal for the amendment was not disclosed in a proxy or information statement filed by it; or registrant determines to change its fiscal year from that used in its most recent SEC filing other than by means of a shareholder vote or an amendment to articles/bylaws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing period: Within 4 business days. S-3 impact: Yes — failure to timely file will impact S-3 eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 5.04 — Temporary suspension of trading under registrant’s employee benefit plans (blackout notifications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrant receives notice of commencement of a blackout period under a company pension plan required by Section 101(i)(2)(E) of ERISA, or, if no receipt of notice, transmission by registrant of a timely notice to an affected officer or director under Rule 104 of Regulation BTR; or registrant transmits a timely updated notice pursuant to Rule 104(b) of Regulation BTR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing period: Within 4 business days after receipt of notice by registrant, or on same date that registrant transmits a timely initial or updated notice pursuant to Rule 104(b)(2)(iii) of Regulation BTR. S-3 impact: Yes — failure to timely file will impact S-3 eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 5.05 — Amendments to code of ethics or waiver of a provision
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrant amends (other than technical/administrative/non-substantive amendments), or grants a waiver (including an implicit waiver) of a provision of its code of ethics identified in Reg S-K Item 406(b) that is applicable to its principal executive officer, principal financial officer, principal accounting officer or controller or persons performing similar functions, unless registrant discloses such amendment or waiver on its internet website as previously indicated in its most recent annual report (including the intention to provide disclosure in this manner).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing period: Within 4 business days. S-3 impact: Yes — failure to timely file will impact S-3 eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 5.06 — Change in shell company status
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrant completes a transaction (if it is a shell company other than a business combination related shell company) that causes it to cease being a shell company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing period: Within 4 business days. S-3 impact: Yes — failure to timely file will impact S-3 eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 5.07 — Submission of matters to a vote of security holders
rubrics_metrics.description: The results of a vote of registrant’s security holders on any matter; registrant’s decision regarding the frequency of shareholder votes on executive compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing period: Initial Form 8-K with preliminary (or final, if available) voting results due within 4 business days after the end of the meeting. Amended Form 8-K due within 4 business days after final voting results are known (if not reported in initial Form 8-K). Amended Form 8-K regarding frequency of shareholder votes due no later than 150 calendar days after the end of the meeting, but no later than 60 days prior to the deadline for submission of shareholder proposals under Rule 14a-8, as disclosed in the registrant’s most recent proxy statement. S-3 impact: Yes — failure to timely file will impact S-3 eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 5.08 — Shareholder director nominations
rubrics_metrics.description: If registrant did not hold an annual meeting in the previous year or if date of this year’s annual meeting has changed by more than 30 days from previous year and registrant is required to include shareholder nominees in its proxy materials due to state/foreign law or governing documents, the determination of the date by which a nominating shareholder or nominating shareholder group must submit a notice on Schedule 14N pursuant to Exchange Act Rule 14a-18.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing period: Within 4 business days after registrant determines the anticipated meeting date. Comment: Less than 100 Form 8-Ks were filed under Item 5.08 in 2021. S-3 impact: Yes — failure to timely file will impact S-3 eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 6 — Asset-Backed Securities items (applicability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Items under section 6 apply only to asset-backed securities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing period: Within 4 business days. S-3 impact: Yes — failure to timely file will impact S-3 eligibility. (Applies only to ABS registrants.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 7.01 — Regulation FD Disclosure (furnished)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrant elects to disclose information through Form 8-K pursuant to Regulation FD that is not disclosed under Item 8.01.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Furnishing period: Simultaneously, in the case of an intentional disclosure, and promptly, in the case of a non-intentional disclosure (see Rule 100 of Regulation FD). S-3 impact: No impact. Note: Item 7.01 disclosures are 'furnished' rather than 'filed.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 8.01 — Other events
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrant elects to disclose any event, with respect to which information is not otherwise required by Form 8-K, that it deems of importance to security holders, including non-public information required to be disclosed by Regulation FD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing period: If solely satisfying obligations under Regulation FD, simultaneously (intentional) or promptly (non-intentional); if other events, at registrant's discretion. S-3 impact: No impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 9.01 — Financial statements and exhibits
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial statements of businesses or funds acquired; pro forma financial information; shell company transactions; exhibits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing period: For business acquisitions and pro forma financial information relative to acquired businesses (other than in shell company transactions), not later than 71 calendar days from the date the initial Form 8-K was required to be filed. Additional timing and exhibit rules apply depending on the transaction type.

rubrics_metrics.name: General note on substituting Form 8-K disclosures in Form 10-K/10-Q
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, a registrant may provide the information required by an item of Form 8-K in the item entitled 'Other Events' in a Form 10-K or Form 10-Q, provided that such Form 10-K or Form 10-Q is filed within four business days of the triggering event that would otherwise require the filing of a Form 8-K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caveat: The SEC takes the position that the item must be reported on a Form 8-K within four business days of the triggering event even if also reported in a Form 10-K or Form 10-Q within four business days of the triggering event.
